title: Carlos Alcaraz Smiled After a 3:34 AM Loss — Here's Why
summary:
Imagine playing a tennis match that ends at 3:34 in the morning. That's what happened to Carlos Alcaraz at the US Open. He lost to Ben Shelton after four hours and 28 minutes. It was the latest finish in the tournament's history.

But here's the surprising part: Alcaraz walked off the court with a huge smile. Why? Because he had been injured for over five months. A wrist injury left him in pain every day. He missed the French Open and Wimbledon. He didn't even know if he could play in New York until a week before.

"I suffered, but I enjoyed, and that's why I smiled," he said. "I missed that feeling."

Alcaraz thinks matches shouldn't go so late. "I think it's too much," he said. He wants a maximum finish time of 11 p.m. Other players also finished after 1 a.m. or 2 a.m.

Alcaraz is 23 years old and has won seven Grand Slam titles. This week, he's playing for Team Europe in the Laver Cup in London. "When you have your team-mates, the best in the world, by your side, it's a weird feeling but it's beautiful," he said.
why_it_matters: It shows that losing isn't the only thing that matters — being able to play at all after months of injury can feel like a win, and it's okay to speak up when something like a super-late schedule seems unfair.
